body_ar:
العلم نور يستضيء به السائرون إلى الله عز وجل، ولهذا كان العلماء هم أهل الخشية والخوف والمراقبة لله عز وجل، وكما قيل: من كان بالله أعرف كان لله أخوف. فيجب على كل مسلم ومسلمة أن يتعلم ما يهمه من أمر دينه، وما يستطيع أن يعبد الله به على بصيرة.
فضل العلم والعلماء:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله عز وجل قد وصف نفسه بالعلم، وأثنى على العلماء من عباده، واستشهد العلماء على أعظم شهادة بعد أن شهد بها وأشهد بها ملائكته، فقال تعالى: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ وَأُوْلُوا الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ [آل عمران:18] ، وأخبر أن العلماء وحدهم هم الذين يخشونه حق خشيته، فقال تعالى: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ [فاطر:28]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Knowledge is a light by which those travelling toward God, mighty and majestic, find their way. For this reason the scholars are the people of awe, of fear and of watchfulness before God, mighty and majestic; and as has been said: whoever knows God better fears God more. So it is obligatory (wājib) upon every Muslim man and every Muslim woman to learn what matters to him of the affair of his religion, and what enables him to worship God with clear sight.

## The merit of knowledge and of the scholars

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: God, mighty and majestic, has described Himself by knowledge, and has praised the scholars among His servants, and has called the scholars to bear witness to the greatest testimony of all — after He had borne witness to it Himself and had His angels bear witness to it. He, exalted is He, said: {God bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those possessed of knowledge, upholding justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:18). And He informed us that the scholars alone are the ones who fear Him as He ought to be feared, for He, exalted is He, said: {It is only those of His servants possessed of knowledge who fear God} (Sūrat Fāṭir 35:28) …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis after the second proof-text, with the merit of knowledge and of the scholars established from scripture but not yet expounded, and with nothing said about the obligation to learn that the synopsis states. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/g-17.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.arabic: فيجب على كل مسلم ومسلمة أن يتعلم ما يهمه من أمر دينه
options: it is obligatory (wājib) upon every Muslim man and every Muslim woman to learn what matters to him
every Muslim man and woman must learn what concerns them
seeking the knowledge one needs is individually obligatory (farḍ ʿayn)
flags.note: A ruling, and the only one in the record; the fixed mapping gives 'obligatory'. The third option has deliberately NOT been taken: the classification of this obligation as individually rather than communally obligatory is the standard scholarly refinement, but the source does not make it and supplying it would be adding a ruling the Sheikh did not give. The whole sentence is in any case the site's synopsis; the transcribed lesson never reaches the question. The Arabic doubles the noun, 'مسلم ومسلمة', and the English keeps the doubling rather than collapsing it into 'every Muslim'.

flags.context: the site's synopsis, on the scholars
options: the people of awe, of fear and of watchfulness
those who possess reverence, fear and mindfulness of God
flags.note: Three distinct words and the English keeps three. 'خشية' is the fear that comes of knowing what one fears, which is why the verse in the transcribed portion attaches it to the scholars; 'خوف' is fear plainly; 'مراقبة' is the awareness of being observed by God. Collapsing them into one English word would destroy the argument, since the whole point is that the first is the scholars' own.

flags.arabic: وأخبر أن العلماء وحدهم هم الذين يخشونه حق خشيته
flags.context: the Sheikh's gloss on Sūrat Fāṭir 35:28
options: keep the gloss visibly his, distinct from the verse it introduces
render the gloss and the verse as one statement
flags.note: The verse says that it is the knowledgeable among God's servants who fear Him. The words 'alone' and 'as He ought to be feared' are the Sheikh's reading of it, not the verse's wording, and the English keeps them in his sentence and out of the braces. This distinction matters generally in this corpus: a gloss that is allowed to migrate into a quotation becomes scripture.

flags.arabic: وكما قيل: من كان بالله أعرف كان لله أخوف
flags.context: the maxim in the site's synopsis
options: keep 'as has been said' and attribute no further
attribute the maxim to its usual source
flags.note: The saying is well known and is variously attributed in the literature of spiritual instruction. The source attributes it to no one — 'as has been said' — and the English does the same, per style guide section 4. The comparative pair 'أعرف / أخوف' is kept as a comparative in the English.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The record's subject overlaps with records 728 ('منهجية في طلب العلم') and 700 of the preceding slice ('آداب طلب العلم'), and all three break off before their substance.

'يستضيء به السائرون إلى الله' is rendered 'by which those travelling toward God find their way'. 'السائرون' is the vocabulary of the spiritual journey; 'wayfarers' was avoided as archaic, and the image of the lamp in the title is carried by 'find their way'.
